summary: Customers in private VPC seeing 403 from IP-based RBAC conditions due to untrusted X-Forwarded-For header from proxy chain
description: Issue summary: Several Soteria Health users in a private VPC deployment report sudden 403 Authorization failures when calling Redwood admin APIs. The errors began after an internal network appliance upgrade. Impact: A subset of service accounts and admin users are blocked from performing operations that are gated by IP-based conditional RBAC rules (e.g., allow-listing corporate IP ranges). Environment: Private deployment (customer-managed VPC) fronted by customer edge proxy + Redwood identity proxy in us-east-1. Steps to reproduce: 1) Call admin endpoint with a request proxied through the customer's upgraded edge appliance. 2) Observe 403 with error 'denied by ip_condition'. 3) Repeat from same client but bypassing edge appliance (direct to Redwood ingress) — request succeeds. Expected behavior: Requests forwarded through trusted proxies should evaluate the original client IP and allow access when within allow-list. Actual behavior: Requests forwarded via the customer's upgraded edge appliance are being evaluated with a spoofed/misattributed client IP (X-Forwarded-For appears to contain internal hop IPs first), causing the RBAC engine's IP condition check to fail. Logs/Traces: AuthN logs show valid JWT and tenant; authZ logs show evaluated ip_condition set to "203.0.113.245" (edge appliance) rather than the original client IP. Ingress proxy provenance trace: received X-Forwarded-For: "10.0.0.5, 203.0.113.245". Identity proxy received the same header without a trusted-hop validation. Customer reports appliance upgrade changelog included "preserve-source-ip=false" by default.
comments: 2026-03-13 09:12 - Customer (Soteria): 'All of our automation that runs from on-prem IPs is failing with 403s after our edge appliance update.'
2026-03-13 09:47 - Support (Elaine Park): 'Thanks — investigating. Can you share a request-id and a sample X-Forwarded-For header from a failing request?'

2026-03-13 13:20 - Engineering (Marco Ruiz): 'Reproduced in staging by inserting a proxy hop that prepends a private RFC1918 address before the public edge IP in XFF. RBAC engine currently trusts the left-most XFF element as source IP when header present.'
2026-03-14 08:21 - SRE (Ivy Chen): 'We applied a workaround to verify proxy-hop trust and prefer the right-most public IP when intermediate hops are private. Rolling to canary.'
investigation_notes: Hypothesis: Identity/ingress proxy accepts X-Forwarded-For without validating trust of upstream hop; upgraded appliance now prepends internal hop which pushes client IP to the right, altering evaluation if trust policy expects left-most client.
Observed authz decision traces: ip_condition evaluated against 203.0.113.245 (edge appliance) not 198.51.100.77 (client) because XFF order changed after appliance rewrite.
Reproduced: Created synthetic proxy that inserts '10.0.0.5' before public IP in XFF; RBAC check fails when trust policy is configured to treat left-most token as client IP.

Configuration review: Some private deployments configure 'trust-proxy=true' without restricting trusted hops; ingress should validate hop IPs against a configured trusted list or use right-most public IP when private hops present.

Related: linked INT-4219 tracks a planned auth library change to XFF parsing and trusted-hop config; PR opened to ingress-proxy to add explicit trusted_hops and to ignore RFC1918 tokens when selecting client IP.
Risk analysis: If we flip selection logic globally without per-tenant config, some customers who rely on left-most semantics may be affected. Need customer-scoped rollback/feature-flag.
resolution_notes: Workaround (applied 2026-03-14): Deployed ingress-proxy canary to Soteria's private control plane that 1) validates X-Forwarded-For hop chain against configured 'trusted_hops' and 2) when private RFC1918 hops are present, prefers the nearest public IP for RBAC evaluation. This restored access for affected service accounts.

Fix plan: Merge PR https://github.com/redwood/ingress-proxy/pull/1124 which introduces tenant-scoped 'trusted_hops' config and a 'xff_selection_policy' parameter ('left-most', 'right-most-public', 'validated-trusted-hops'). Ship as opt-in for private deployments with follow-up migration docs.

Post-deploy actions: 1) Add runbook instructions to validate edge appliance XFF behavior during upgrades. 2) Notify customers in private tier with IP-based RBAC to review 'trusted_hops' config. 3) Schedule postmortem and update RBAC docs.

Customer follow-up: Soteria Health confirmed workaround fixed immediate blocking issue and will coordinate with their appliance vendor to preserve original-source-ip semantics or explicitly configure proxy to forward XFF in expected order.
Closure criteria: Fix merged and enabled in customer's control plane, runbook updated, automated tests added to prevent regressions.
